title: Lesson 16. Functions
description: Declaring and calling, parameters, return, arrow functions

learn.intro: Hi! Lesson 16 — **functions**. A function is a recipe: you describe it once, and then say «cook it» as many times as you want. Let's go!

slides.text: You've already used a function: `console.log()` is a function someone wrote for us. Now let's learn to write **our own**.
Declaring a function:

`function` — «a recipe is coming».
`greet` — the function's name, we call it by this.
`(name)` — a parameter, the ingredient that will be passed in.
`{ ... }` — the recipe steps.
`return` — the finished dish the function gives back.
If you run only the declaration — nothing appears in the console. We wrote the recipe but haven't cooked anything yet.

check.prompt: The word return is the function's name.
check.explain: The name is greet. return gives the result back.

check.prompt: What is name in function greet(name)?
check.explain: Parameters go in the parentheses of the declaration.

slides.text: For a function to run, you need to **call** it — write its name and parentheses:
slides.code:
console.log(greet("Anya")); // Hello, Anya
console.log(greet("Aziz")); // Hello, Aziz

slides.text:
**Declaration** — writing the recipe, once: `function greet(name) { ... }`.
**Call** — cooking by the recipe, as many times as you want: `greet("Anya")`.
The word function and curly braces — it's a declaration. Just a name and parentheses — it's a call.

check.prompt: How many times can you call one function?
check.explain: The recipe is written once, and you can cook from it any number of times.
"Ali" is put in place of name.

slides.text:
A **parameter** is a blank line in the recipe: «take ___ of meat». It's written in the declaration.
An **argument** is what you actually put in: «500 grams of beef». It's written in the call.
There can be several parameters — separated by commas:
`return` gives back the result. Without it, the function gives nothing:
The recipe did something but didn't hand over the dish — that's why it's undefined.

pairs: What the function expects (in the declaration)

check.prompt: A function can have several parameters separated by commas.

slides.text: This isn't a new topic — it's the same function, just written **shorter**. You'll see it very often in modern code.
Three ways to write the same thing:
If you paste all three versions into the console at once, you'll get the error «has already been declared»: the name greet is taken. Try them one at a time and refresh the page (F5).

check.prompt: How can this function be shortened?
check.explain: One parameter — no parentheses; only return — no { } and no return.

slides.text: The main idea is **don't repeat code**. Without a function, the same thing is written three times, and changing the text means editing three places. And what if there are 100 people?
With a function, the recipe is written once:
A function + the loop from lesson 15 — and you can greet even 100 people:
Now the text is in one place: change it in the function — it changes everywhere.

check.prompt: If you change the text inside welcome, it changes in every call.
check.explain: There's one recipe — every call cooks from it.

slides.text: A sum function — takes two numbers and returns their sum:
Trap: sum("2", 3) returns "23", not 5. Text plus a number get glued together — remember lesson 13?

Homework: a function `isEven(number)` returns `true` for an even number and `false` for an odd one. Code in `script.js`, the result through `return`, call it at least 3 times. Hint: the `%` operator. Bonus — as a one-line arrow function.

questions.explain: Someone wrote it for us, and we call it.

questions.prompt: Match the part of a function and its meaning
What appears in the console if you run only this code?
questions.explain: This is only a declaration — the recipe is written but not called.

questions.prompt: Which line is a function call?
questions.explain: A call is a name and parentheses, without the word function.

questions.prompt: In the call greet("Anya"), the string "Anya" is…
questions.explain: An argument is what's passed in the call.

options: My name is name, I'm age
questions.explain: Arguments are filled in order: name = "Ali", age = 15.
No return — the function gives nothing back.

questions.prompt: Without return, a function still gives back its result.
questions.explain: Without return the result is undefined.

questions.prompt: Which one is an arrow function?
questions.explain: An arrow function is written with =>.

questions.prompt: Build a short arrow function for a sum
With two parameters you can drop the parentheses: a, b => a + b
questions.explain: Parentheses are dropped only with one parameter. Correct: (a, b) => a + b.

questions.prompt: What is the main idea of functions?
questions.explain: Write the recipe once and use it as much as you want.
Text plus a number get glued into a string.

questions.prompt: What should isEven(number) return so it's true for even numbers?
questions.explain: An even number has remainder 0 when divided by 2.
